items.prompt: A complete recursive story must name?
choices: Base case, smaller subproblem, and what the stack holds
A hash map of all frames
items.whyRight: Without those three, the algorithm is hand-wavy.
whyWrong: Base alone does not shrink the problem.
Maps are optional memo tools, not the definition.

choices: The recursive call is the final action of the function
The function never returns a value
items.whyRight: Nothing happens after the call returns — compilers may reuse the frame.
whyWrong: Values can still return through the tail call.
Two calls usually break tail form.

items.prompt: Deep recursion on large n risks?
items.whyRight: Each frame consumes stack until the base returns.

items.prompt: Converting recursion to iteration often uses an explicit?
choices: Stack (or rewriting as a loop with your own state)
Only a queue of random nodes
items.whyRight: You simulate the call stack or find a closed loop form.

choices: Overlapping subproblems repeat the same arguments
The graph is a pure tree with no repeats
You only need the base case
items.whyRight: Caching repeated argument tuples avoids exponential rework.
whyWrong: Unique subproblems gain little from a cache.
Trees without overlap need no memo.
Base cases alone do not motivate memo tables.

items.prompt: Mutual recursion (A calls B calls A) still needs?
choices: A reachable base that stops the cycle of calls
items.whyRight: Some path must hit a case that does not call onward.
whyWrong: Parameters usually carry the shrinking measure.
Globals are a poor substitute for clear base cases.
